name: the-living-atlas
title: The Living Atlas
question: Do all of the paper's semantic figures actually compile to executables that run, and — the real test of composition — can the independently-authored figure mechanisms be assembled into a single whole cell that lives the paper's full arc: grow, divide, and die?
biological_summary: This is the payoff. The nine figure studies each showed one pattern compiling from draft to executable; this study shows the whole atlas running at once and, more importantly, composing. The gallery renders the dynamics of all twelve executables side by side — each compiled figure, actually moving. Then the figures are assembled into a single cell. It takes up nutrients and grows (biomass peaking at ≈ 8.4); as it grows it divides (cell_count 1 → 14); and when a thermal shock pushes its temperature to 50° — outside the viable band — it loses viability (→ ≈0), stops maintaining its boundary, and disintegrates into molecular debris (→ 7.3), with mass conserved through death (peak biomass 8.4 → debris 7.3). The paper's arc — interface, coupling, metabolism, closure, division, disintegration — runs end to end in one composite. A cell, assembled from drafts, that lives and dies.
claim: The patterns compose: independently-specified interfaces and mechanisms can be assembled into one cell that lives the paper's full arc.

conclusion:
## Claims
- The composed whole cell runs the full arc in ONE conserved trajectory: autocatalytic growth to biomass 8.4 (dividing to 14 cells), then a thermal shock ramps temperature past tolerance, viability collapses, and biomass converts to molecular debris (7.3) — mass conserved through death (biomass → debris).

## Evidence
- **FULL-ARC** — growth, division, shock, death, debris in one composite
- **MASS-CONSERVED-THROUGH-DEATH** — peak biomass 8.4 → debris 7.3 (conserved)
- **VIABILITY-CLIFF** — viability 1.0 → ~0 at the shock
- **DIVIDES** — cell_count 1 → 14 before death
- **conservation** — mass conserved through death: peak biomass 8.43 → debris 7.26; divides to 14 cells; viability -0.00

## Limitations
- Composed toy-real cell: mass is conserved through the full arc, but it reuses illustrative handlers and is not a calibrated whole-cell model.

## Next steps
- Run the composed cell across replicate seeds and environments to move from a single arc to a distribution of outcomes.
